claim: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology seeks to address growing concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replications of selected experiments from high-profile papers in cancer biology.
source: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology seeks to address growing concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replications of selected experiments from a number of high-profile papers in the field of cancer biology.
evidence: This is a stated objective of the project described in the abstract.

claim: The papers selected for replication were published between 2010 and 2012.
source: The papers, which were published between 2010 and 2012, were selected on the basis of citations and Altmetric scores (Errington et al., 2014).
evidence: Direct statement with citation to Errington et al., 2014.

claim: Peinado and colleagues published 'Melanoma exosomes educate bone marrow progenitor cells toward a pro-metastatic phenotype through MET' in Nature Medicine in 2012.
source: This Registered Report describes the proposed replication plan of key experiments from "Melanoma exosomes educate bone marrow progenitor cells toward a pro-metastatic phenotype through MET" by Peinado and colleagues, published in Nature Medicine in 2012 (Peinado et al., 2012).
evidence: Direct statement with citation to Peinado et al., 2012.

claim: Tumor exosomes enhance metastasis to bones and lungs.
source: In these experiments, Peinado and colleagues show tumor exosomes enhance metastasis to bones and lungs, which is diminished by reducing Met expression in exosomes (Peinado et al., 2012).
evidence: Statement attributed to Peinado et al., 2012 findings.

claim: Reducing Met expression in exosomes diminishes exosome-enhanced metastasis to bones and lungs.
source: In these experiments, Peinado and colleagues show tumor exosomes enhance metastasis to bones and lungs, which is diminished by reducing Met expression in exosomes (Peinado et al., 2012).

claim: The replication attempt will not include the FACS sorting step used in the original protocol.
source: The original protocol for selecting GFP-positive cells included a step to perform fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) of the population to achieve a 95–99% GFP-positive population prior to puromycin selection (information provided by authors). The replication attempt will not include the FACS sorting step and instead will select the stable cells for at least 28 d before further analysis and will maintain the cell lines when not used in experimental procedures under puromycin selection.
evidence: Direct statement of a known difference from the original study.
